info.name: CellularFX
info.comment: Generates cellular (Worley) noise for stone, foam, cracks, cells and similar textures.

description.p: CellularFX is a source effect that takes no input. It places one feature point in every cell of an unbounded lattice and derives each output sample from the distances between the sample and its nearest features. The result fills the primitive subregion, and every sample depends only on its position in primitive units. Clipped, partial and full redraws therefore produce identical values.

The lattice is defined by CellWidth and CellHeight, positioned by OriginX and OriginY, and rotated by Angle. Percentages in these fields refer to the filter region, so CellWidth = 12.5% gives eight cells across it. Each feature is displaced from its cell centre by up to Jitter, and the positions, heights and cell values are chosen by Seed. Distances are measured in lattice units, in which one cell measures 1 × 1, and WorleyMetric selects the distance function.

WorleyMode selects how the distances are converted to a value. F1, F2 and F2_F1 produce distances to the nearest features, WEIGHTED and PEAKS combine distances with the seeded feature heights from HeightMin to HeightMax, and CELL gives each cell a constant seeded value in [0, 1). Values are not normalised against the drawn area, and the range of each mode is described in WorleyMode.

Octaves sums independently seeded layers, each sampled Lacunarity times more finely than the last and weighted by Persistence. The sum is divided by the total weight, so several octaves stay within the range of a single octave. PeriodX and PeriodY make the pattern repeat after a whole number of cells.

In IMAGE mode, values are clamped to [0, 1] and drawn as opaque greyscale, or through the colour ramp of ColourMap or Stops. Set OutputMode to HEIGHT to produce an unclamped floating-point scalar field for numerical inputs, such as the height map of an enhanced LightingFX or the amount mask of a CompositeFX. Prefer HEIGHT for lighting, because the 8-bit greyscale of IMAGE output produces visible terraces.

Greyscale output is written in the effect's colour space. In a linear RGB filter, which is the SVG default, values are therefore treated as linear light and appear brighter once they are converted for display. For example, 0.25 is displayed as 135 rather than 64. Draw the effect in an sRGB filter to display values directly. Colour ramps are drawn as authored in either colour space.

Some combinations of fields can only be checked when the effect is drawn, because fields may be set in any order. CELL with more than one octave, a period with an Angle that is not a multiple of 360, and a periodic octave stack with a non-integer Lacunarity each cause the effect to draw nothing. Draw then logs a warning and returns ERR::InvalidValue. Draw also returns ERR::OutOfRange if the lattice coordinates of the drawn area would exceed 2^52, beyond which cell positions are not exact.
Samples are taken once at each pixel centre, so the hard edges of CELL and F2_F1 output are not antialiased.
SVG documents can use the effect with the xvg:feCellular element. Refer to the SVG class for its attributes.

action.name: Draw
action.comment: Render the effect to the target bitmap.
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.
The Y position of the region to be drawn.
The width of the region to be drawn.
The height of the region to be drawn.

description.p: Draw fails with ERR::InvalidValue if CELL mode is combined with more than one octave, if a periodic pattern is rotated, or if a periodic pattern of several octaves has a fractional Lacunarity. It fails with ERR::OutOfRange if the drawn area lies so far from the origin, at the finest octave, that cell indices can no longer be represented exactly.

field.name: Angle
field.comment: Rotates the lattice clockwise about its origin, in degrees.

description.p: The rotation is applied about the point given by OriginX and OriginY. The value must be finite and defaults to 0. A periodic pattern cannot be rotated: if PeriodX or PeriodY is set, the Angle must be a multiple of 360 or the effect will fail to draw.

field.name: CellHeight
field.comment: The vertical spacing of the base lattice.

description.p: The value must be finite and greater than zero. A percentage refers to the height of the filter region. The default is 12.5%, which gives eight rows of cells within the filter region.
Distances are measured in cell units, so cells of different width and height stretch the distance metric with them.

field.name: CellWidth
field.comment: The horizontal spacing of the base lattice.

description.p: The value must be finite and greater than zero. A percentage refers to the width of the filter region. The default is 12.5%, which gives eight columns of cells within the filter region.

field.name: ColourMap
field.comment: Draws IMAGE output through a pre-defined colour ramp.

description.p: The clamped value of each sample selects a colour from the named colourmap, from the first colour at 0 to the last at 1. The following colourmaps from the matplotlib and seaborn projects are supported: cmap:crest, cmap:flare, cmap:icefire, cmap:inferno, cmap:magma, cmap:mako, cmap:plasma, cmap:rocket, cmap:viridis.
Setting a colourmap replaces custom Stops. Set an empty string to clear the ramp and draw in greyscale. HEIGHT output ignores the ramp. Unknown names fail with ERR::NotFound.

field.name: HeightMax
field.comment: The highest seeded feature height, for the WEIGHTED and PEAKS modes.

description.p: Each feature is given a height between HeightMin and HeightMax, in cell units. The value must lie in the range [-4, 4] and defaults to 1. If HeightMax is lower than HeightMin, the two are swapped when drawing.

field.name: HeightMin
field.comment: The lowest seeded feature height, for the WEIGHTED and PEAKS modes.

description.p: The value must lie in the range [-4, 4] and defaults to 0. See HeightMax.

field.name: Jitter
field.comment: The maximum displacement of each feature from its cell centre, as a fraction of the cell.

description.p: A value of 0 places every feature at its cell centre, giving a regular grid of square or rectangular cells. A value of 1, the default, allows a feature to lie anywhere within its cell. The value must lie in the range [0, 1].

field.name: Lacunarity
field.comment: The frequency multiplier between octaves.

description.p: Each octave samples the lattice Lacunarity times more finely than the previous one. The value must lie in the range [1, 8] and defaults to 2. A periodic pattern of more than one octave requires an integer value, or the effect will fail to draw.

field.name: Octaves
field.comment: The number of independently seeded layers.

description.p: Each octave is sampled at Lacunarity times the frequency of the previous one and weighted by Persistence relative to it. The weighted sum is divided by the total weight, so several octaves stay within the range of one. The value must lie in the range [1, 12] and defaults to 1. The CELL mode supports one octave only.

field.name: OriginX
field.comment: The horizontal origin of the lattice, relative to the left edge of the filter region.

description.p: A percentage refers to the width of the filter region. The value must be finite and defaults to 0. Moving the origin translates the pattern without changing it, and Angle rotates the lattice about this point.

field.name: OriginY
field.comment: The vertical origin of the lattice, relative to the top edge of the filter region.

description.p: A percentage refers to the height of the filter region. The value must be finite and defaults to 0.

field.name: OutputMode
field.comment: Selects an image or a floating-point scalar result.

description.p: IMAGE, the default, draws clamped greyscale or colour-mapped pixels. HEIGHT writes the unclamped field values to a scalar surface for numerical inputs and ignores the colour ramp. A height cannot be the final result of a filter, so a HEIGHT effect must be read by a later effect. NATIVE is unsupported.

field.name: PeriodX
field.comment: Repeats the pattern horizontally after this number of base cells.

description.p: The pattern repeats exactly every PeriodX * CellWidth, with no seam. The value must lie in the range [0, 1048576], and 0, the default, disables horizontal repetition. A periodic pattern cannot be rotated, and a periodic pattern of several octaves requires an integer Lacunarity.

field.name: PeriodY
field.comment: Repeats the pattern vertically after this number of base cells.

description.p: The value must lie in the range [0, 1048576], and 0, the default, disables vertical repetition. See PeriodX.

field.name: Persistence
field.comment: The weight of each octave relative to the previous one.

description.p: Octave k is weighted by Persistence^k. The value must lie in the range [0, 1] and defaults to 0.5. A value of 0 leaves only the first octave.

field.name: Seed
field.comment: Selects the feature positions, heights and cell values.

description.p: Any 64-bit value is accepted, including 0, which is the default. The same seed always produces the same pattern.

field.name: Stops
field.comment: Draws IMAGE output through a custom colour ramp.

description.p: The clamped value of each sample selects a colour from the gradient defined by the stops. At least two stops are required, or the setter fails with ERR::InvalidValue.
Setting stops replaces any named ColourMap. Set an empty array to clear the ramp and draw in greyscale. HEIGHT output ignores the ramp.

field.name: WorleyMetric
field.comment: Selects the distance metric.

description.p: EUCLIDEAN (the default) gives rounded cells, MANHATTAN gives diamond-shaped contours and CHEBYSHEV gives square contours. Distances are measured in cell units.

field.name: WorleyMode
field.comment: Selects how distances to the nearest features are converted to a value.

description.p: Distances are in cell units and are not normalised against the drawn area. With F1 the distance to the nearest feature is used, and with F2 the distance to the second-nearest. F2_F1 is their difference, which is zero on the boundaries between cells and suits cracks and mortar. WEIGHTED is the minimum over all features of the distance less the feature's height, and PEAKS is the maximum of the height less the distance. CELL gives every sample the seeded value of its nearest feature, which is constant within each cell and lies in [0, 1).

With the default Jitter of 1, F1 rarely exceeds 0.8 under the Euclidean metric, and F2 can exceed 1. On a regular grid (Jitter 0), F1 reaches about 0.707, 1 or 0.5 at cell corners under the Euclidean, Manhattan and Chebyshev metrics, and F2 is 1 at a cell centre under every metric. WEIGHTED and PEAKS may be negative. IMAGE output clamps every mode to [0, 1]; use a colour ramp, RemapFX or HEIGHT output to work with other ranges.
The CELL mode supports one octave only.
